display_name: Zelda II: The Adventure of Link
subtitle: BizHawk
_subtitle_source: subtitle names the backend the player runs, as in 18 other manifests.
_platform_source: The game is a NES cartridge, and our own world targets it there: worlds/zelda2 reads the NES work RAM through London's BizHawk connector. Every other release of Zelda II (GameCube Collector's Edition, Classic NES Series on GBA, Virtual Console, Switch Online) is this same NES ROM inside an emulator, so NES is not one option among several -- it is the only form the game exists in.
ap_world_name: Zelda II: The Adventure of Link
_ap_world_name_source: OUR OWN world declares it: Zelda2-Archipelago worlds/zelda2/__init__.py, `game = "Zelda II: The Adventure of Link"`, and worlds/zelda2/archipelago.json carries the same string. Confirmed end to end by generating 25 seeds against Archipelago 0.6.7, which resolves a world by exactly this name.
description: Zelda II: The Adventure of Link as a multiworld. 116 locations across Hyrule's overworld, towns and seven palaces are shuffled into the session, with the goal, the crystal requirement, key placement and the item pool all configurable. Requires the player's own NES cartridge dump (USA).
_description_source: written by us from our own world's structure -- the location count is the built table in worlds/zelda2/data/apworld_data.json, and the options are the ones Options.py actually declares. No text is copied from the game.
_checks_verified_note: FALSE, and the reason is specific rather than the usual not-yet. Two real pickups were watched live in BizHawk on 25 Aug 2026 and the model reproduced both exactly ($681 bit 3 -> Palaces area 3 screen 0; $615 bit 1 -> West Hyrule area 43 screen 2). But 38 of the 116 locations still depend on one undecided rule in the area-stream walk and may be watching the wrong bit. Those 38 are flagged in the data, carried to the client in slot_data, and the Lua module says so in the log the first time one of them fires. One more measured pickup at any of them settles it for all 38.
_checks_verified_source: measured: Zelda2-Archipelago/tools/presence_log_2026-08-25.txt, and pinned as a regression test in tools/prove_measurements.py. What is NOT measured: that all 116 fire correctly, and that a check reaches the server through London end to end.
_requires_source: NES cartridge title. The player supplies their own dump; nothing of the game is distributed here, and the patch is useless without it.

rom.description: Your own Zelda II: The Adventure of Link cartridge dump for NES -- the USA release. Both the iNES and NES 2.0 header forms are accepted; they are the same cartridge
rom._description_source: our own patcher's rule, worlds/zelda2/Rom.py: identity is the MD5 of PRG+CHR with the 16-byte header excluded, so the two header forms the same dump circulates under are both accepted. A whole-file hash would have refused one of them for a difference that is not in the game.
rom._md5_source: MEASURED from the project owner's own cartridge dump 25 Aug 2026, and cross-checked: rebuilding the iNES v1 header over the same data reproduces 764d36fa8a2450834da5e8194281035a, the hash Zelda 2 Redux's ReadMe documents for the base ROM. ⚠ This is the HEADERLESS hash -- see rom.description.
rom._size_note: Not recorded. The same cartridge is 262144 bytes headerless and 262160 with either header, so a single size would reject a valid dump. The MD5 above is the stronger check and does not have that problem.

emulator.name: BizHawk
emulator._source: London's own NES bridge runs on BizHawk, and 2.9.1 is the floor Archipelago's BizHawk connector states. Our RAM map uses the "RAM" and "PRG ROM" domains, both present since well before that version.

client.name: London
client._name_source: London itself carries the checks for this game -- there is no separate client to start. Our world ships no Component of its own.
client._kind_source: OUR world does not register an Archipelago client: Zelda2-Archipelago worlds/zelda2/__init__.py contains no components.append(Component(...)). London reads the game's memory itself through its own RAM map, which is the kind=london contract.
client._lua_note: Rule 2 satisfied 25 Aug 2026: Plugins/Scripts/games/zelda2.lua is GENERATED by Zelda2-Archipelago/tools/build_lua_map.py from the same table the patcher writes, so the address the client watches and the byte the patch sets cannot drift apart. Proven 23/23 against synthetic memory including the false-goal-at-boot case, and green through lint_lua_domains, lint_goal_guard and BootGarbageCheck.

apworld._source: our own repository. ⚠ NOT PUBLISHED YET -- this address is where it will live; the manifest must not be built into a release before the repository exists, or the store link is a live 404.
apworld._minimum_ap_version_source: worlds/zelda2/archipelago.json. Generation is verified against 0.6.7, which is what the project's own engine runs.

_patch_extension_source: our own patcher, worlds/zelda2/Rom.py: the patch is a list of (offset, bytes) tokens and defines NO APPatchExtension. That is a deliberate limit -- a world that declares its own Python patch steps hands the launcher work it cannot verify, and two games in this catalogue already have to be played unpatched for exactly that reason.
_patch_note: There is deliberately no `patch` block naming an external producer: London builds the patch itself from the seed, using only generic token application. Every location's byte offset was verified against the real cartridge dump -- all 116 hold exactly the item code the extraction predicted.

world_by.name: solida1987
world_by._authors_source: this world is our own work.
world_by._source: written from FiendsOfTheElements/z2disassembly (CC0-1.0), the game's public-domain disassembly. SOURCES.md in that repository records what was used and what was deliberately never read.

credits._game_by_note: Not recorded rather than guessed. The game is Nintendo's and is never distributed here; the player supplies their own cartridge dump.

_removal_note: ⚠ READ THIS BEFORE TOUCHING THIS MANIFEST. The title 'Zelda II: The Adventure of Link' is in catalog/removed.json: an author asked us to withdraw HER world for this game on 20 Aug 2026, and we did -- manifest, package, release asset and RAM map. This is a DIFFERENT world, written from scratch from a public-domain disassembly, and the removal gate lets it through on AUTHORSHIP rather than on the title: credits.world_by.name must be solida1987. Hers names someone else and stays blocked by the same comparison. Negative-tested -- see tools/lint_removed_games.py.
